title: Mushroom Soup
subtitle: Creamy soup of chestnut and dried porcini mushrooms
excerpt: A smooth, intensely savoury mushroom soup made with a blend of fresh chestnut and dried porcini mushrooms, finished with cream and a little thyme. A simple soup with deep flavour.

recipe.sourceNotes: Mushroom soup is one of the few soups that gains greatly from a small quantity of dried mushrooms added to a much larger quantity of fresh: the dried porcini, once soaked, contribute an intensity of flavour that fresh mushrooms cannot match on their own. The soaking liquid, strained through a fine sieve to remove grit, becomes the stock base and should not be discarded. The combination of fresh and dried mushrooms in a creamy, blended soup is associated particularly with French and British cafe and restaurant cooking from the 1970s onwards, when cream soups became fashionable and dried porcini became more widely available in delicatessens. The soup should be blended smooth and then strained if a very fine texture is desired, though a slightly textured result from blending alone is equally good. A few sauteed mushroom slices reserved and placed on top with a thread of cream are a simple but effective garnish.

recipeTools.notes: A large saucepan for the soup.

content.text: Fry the fresh mushrooms over high heat in batches: crowding the pan traps steam and the mushrooms boil rather than fry, producing a watery, pale soup. Each batch should be dark golden before adding the next. Reserve a handful of the fried mushrooms for the garnish. The porcini soaking liquid is the concentrated flavour base: pour it in carefully, stopping before the gritty sediment at the bottom reaches the pan.

items.preparation: soaked in 250 ml boiling water for 20 minutes

content.text: Strain the porcini through a sieve lined with kitchen paper, reserving the soaking liquid. Chop the porcini roughly. Heat the butter and oil in a large saucepan over high heat. Fry the fresh mushrooms in batches until deep golden. Set a handful aside for garnish.

Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and soften for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute. Return all the mushrooms and the chopped porcini. Add the strained porcini liquid and the stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15 minutes.
Blend until smooth. Stir in the cream. Season. Reheat gently. Serve in warm bowls with the reserved mushrooms, a swirl of cream, and a little black pepper.
